description: Horizon mask and Sun / Earth paths seen from the IM-2 Athena landing site.

site.name: IM-2 Athena
site.coordinate_source: LROC (NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera), 'IM-2 Athena Seen Obliquely' (10 Mar 2025): 84.7906 S, 29.1957 E

conventions.altitude: degrees above the local horizontal plane
conventions.frame: MOON_ME_DE421 (Mean Earth / Polar Axis), JPL DE421 ephemeris, apparent positions
conventions.above_horizon: centre of the body is above the terrain horizon (mask_deg) in its direction
conventions.any_part_above_horizon: Earth only: the upper edge of the disk (alt_deg + radius_deg) is above the terrain horizon in the direction of its centre
conventions.radius_deg: Earth only: angular radius of the Earth's disk

mask.dem_source: PGDA product 90, Barker et al. 2023 (LOLA, MOON_ME / DE421, south polar stereographic)
mask.note: Athena rests in a crater about 20 m across. The 10 m elevation grid does not resolve it, so the mask is the horizon of the landing area, not the view from the crater floor.

landing_source: Intuitive Machines news release, 6 Mar 2025: Athena landed 'at approximately 11:30 a.m. CST' (= 17:30 UTC); NASA release 7 Mar 2025: 'touched down at approximately 11:30 a.m. March 6'

actual.source: NASA news release, 7 Mar 2025, 'NASA Receives Some Data Before Intuitive Machines Ends Lunar Mission': 'an early end of mission at 12:15 a.m. CST Friday' (= 06:15 UTC, 7 Mar 2025)

planned.source: NASA CLPS IM-2 press kit (NP-2025-02-005-JSC), Major Mission Milestones and Timeline: 'Surface Operations: Approximately 10 days'

lunar_day.source: One synodic month (29.5 days) from touchdown, for animation; not a mission date.
